segments.description: Up next is Nina Nitinger, founder of Creative Kids Tennis and a licensed Kids Tennis Specialist with Swiss Tennis. Nina brings a wealth of expertise, holding top certifications in tennis and conditioning in Germany and Switzerland. Today she'll present creative approaches to kids tennis, drawing from an extensive background in sports psychology and her work as an expert in kids and junior tennis development. Let's welcome Nina. Hello and good morning from Switzerland. My name is Nina Nitinger and first of all I would like to thank Tennis Australia for giving me the chance to do a presentation here at this virtual conference. It's a great honor for me to be part of this fantastic event. I used to be a professional tennis player and after an injury I had to stop playing and I studied business, sports and sports psychology at university and I have done several certifications in tennis, fitness and mental training. Right now I'm working for the Swiss Tennis Federation in the educational team and I'm the author of some books about mental training, kids tennis and fitness training. Welcome to my presentation about creative kids tennis lessons to improve learning. First of all I would like to talk about what kids really need to have a better chance of learning. Then I would like to talk about game-based learning and explicit versus implicit learning. Then I will talk about the advantages

move the net around and play over the net very good let's talk about explicit versus implicit learning explicit learning as you can see on the picture is the top of the iceberg it's what you can see and implicit learning is what is below the surface it is something you cannot really see explicit learning means the coach is giving children detailed instructions about how to do something the coach gives information about the skill and how to consciously control the movement so the kids know exactly what and how they have to do it implicit learning means the coach is telling the kids what they have to do but the coach does not say how they have to do it they have to solve the problem themselves and they have to find a solution themselves implicit learning is the learning of complex information in an unintentional manner without awareness of what has been learned the kids just learn along the way here is an overview for explicit and implicit learning so explicit learning is always the how it is conscious controlled and visible and we can also talk about the hard skills implicit learning on the other hand is always about the what it is unconscious automatic invisible and holistic and we can also talk about the soft skills there have been 10 studies about implicit and explicit learning and seven out of these 10 studies have showed that implicit learning resulted in better athletic performance and success and it is proven that
